newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: GOLF - STRUVER FOLLOWS IN FOOTSTEPS OF IDOL LANGER.
newsitem.headline: GOLF - STRUVER FOLLOWS IN FOOTSTEPS OF IDOL LANGER.

text.p: German Sven Struver landed the Dutch Open by three strokes on Sunday to follow in the footsteps of his idol and compatriot Bernhard Langer.

Struver began a windy final round sharing a two-shot lead with Englishman Russell Claydon but a second eagle by the German, who holed a 20ft putt on the long 12th, opened up a three-stroke advantage which he held until the end.
Struver's five-under-par 66 for an 18-under 269 gave him his second European Tour title, leaving Claydon with his sixth runners-up spot in professional events, his third on the European Tour.
A 69 by Claydon left him two ahead of compatriot Roger Chapman and Argentina's Angel Cabrera, with another Argentine, Jose Coceres, and England's Richard Boxall a further stroke back.
Coceres lifted himself up the field with the third albatross of the European Tour season when he hit a four-iron second shot 210 yards for his ball to find the cup on the par-five fifth.
Another spectacular shot came from Spain's Pedro Linhart whose eight-iron found the cup for a hole-in-one on the 13th to earn himself a bicycle. A car was on offer two holes later.
However, it was a putt which proved the most important shot of the day, Struver's 25-footer for eagle on the long 12th.
It ended Claydon's chances of catching him once and for all, enabling the German to add his name on the Dutch trophy to Langer's, who won this event in 1984 and 1992.
"Obviously it was the turning-point," said Struver, who included an eagle on the fourth and two birdies, one at the last. "I just had to be steady after that.

"I'm really proud of the way I finished and proud to shoot four rounds in the 60s which I don't think I've done before, but most of all I'm proud to have my name on a trophy which has Bernhard Langer's name on it twice."
The son of a Hamburg golf professional, Struver sprang into the European Tour limelight when his 62 briefly gave him the 1989 German Open lead while an amateur.

However, his most significant feat before the Dutch success was his 63 in the final round of the European Tour-sanctioned South African PGA Championship last year to deny Ernie Els victory on home soil.
Claydon lost a playoff to compatriot Lee Westwood in the Scandinavian Masters just over a year ago.
This is his third European Tour second place and one of his other three runner-up spots was to Greg Norman in the 1989 Australian Masters when still an amateur.
